Why VAPs are not classical autophagy receptors

Canonical autophagy receptors (e.g. p62/SQSTM1, NBR1, OPTN, NDP52) share key features:

Bind cargo (often ubiquitinated)

Bind ATG8/LC3 proteins via a functional LIR (LC3-interacting region)

Direct cargo into autophagosomes

VAPs (VAPA and VAPB):

Are ER membrane proteins

Function primarily as tethers and adaptors at membrane contact sites

Bind many partners via FFAT or FFAT-like motifs

Do not bind autophagic cargo directly in the way receptors do

author: ValWood
body:
If this is the source of the rule, ARBA needs to remove any rules like this. 

Annotations can't be deepened because they have a less specific version of an MF that is usually involved in a process. It might be a different context.

author: Antonialock
body:
ARBA doesn't make inferences like that, it only propagates exact GO terms (or parents) based on existing annotation. 

It looks like the pombe proteins used to be annotated to this term using IPI evidence PomBase source, and it disappeared between our version 132 and 133 of this entry:
https://www.uniprot.org/uniprotkb/Q10484/history?versions=132%2C133

Abdu says that the annotation will be gone from the next update early April (26_02), apologies for the delay, I don't understand why it is so slow!
